text:
Dallas got the bigger first period and had one goal to show for it. The Stars piled up 1.37 expected goals to Colorado's 0.64 in the opening 20 minutes, yet it was the Avalanche who led for most of it, on Artturi Lehkonen's backhand at 11:32. Tyler Seguin tied it on the power play with 54 seconds left in the period, a snap shot that carried only an 8 percent chance of scoring. Then the game turned. Colorado outplayed Dallas in the second (1.27 to 0.92) and flattened them in the third (1.40 to 0.34).

Martin Necas supplied the separation. He scored at 3:05 of the second with a slap shot, then added a power-play snap at 16:14 that made it 3-1. Necas logged 23.4 minutes, and Colorado generated 1.38 expected goals with him on the ice against just 0.27 allowed. Nathan MacKinnon set up the first of those goals and finished with two assists, and the Avalanche kept Dallas's shots to the outside, blocking 19 to the Stars' 6.

Dallas made it close. Roope Hintz cut the deficit to one at 3:17 of the third, and the Stars outshot Colorado 59 to 47 in attempts, but the quality of chances never matched the volume. Seguin put seven shots on net, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 24 of 26, 0.63 goals better than expected. Jake Oettinger was close to average. Colorado deserved to win 55 percent of the time, and it did.
